findings.reason: a coordinator reading the followup dispatches §3 and §4 in parallel into `reckon/_store.py`, and the merge of two concurrent edits to one function is exactly what the declared waits are for.
findings.text: §4 writes `reckon/_store.py` (for `data-evidence-origin` in `_evidence_section_html`), and so does §3 (line 45), yet §4's only declared wait is on §2 and the followup at line 57 tells the coordinator the two "can then run together" — two concurrent nodes would hold one file, which is the overlap the same paragraph's §2 waits exist to prevent

findings.reason: the rule the implementer writes from is an id test that misses a class of generated id the synthesis actually produces, so the node's third case passes while the record gains a duplicate anchored section.
findings.text: §4's legacy rule classifies an unmarked section as appended when its id is neither one of the plan's section ids nor `outcome`, but `_render_document` builds `available` from the plan's comment keys and from each ledger run's `section` key (`reckon/evidence.py:340-354`), so it also generates ids that are not plan headings; an unmarked section under such an id (a comment or run anchored to a section since removed from the plan) is therefore both carried forward as "appended" and generated again, publishing the same id twice
